title: Statistics - Lesson 1: Reading Statistical Reports Practice
description: Practice identifying claims, sources, displays, statistics, and evidence-based conclusions.

questions.question: A report says, "Most surveyed learners prefer video lessons." What part of the report is this sentence?
questions.explanation: The sentence is the main statement the report wants the reader to believe, so it is the claim.

questions.question: A survey asked 50 learners, and 32 chose video lessons. What percent chose video lessons?
A conclusion should name the group or source that the statistic describes.
questions.explanation: Naming the group prevents the conclusion from describing more people than the data actually measured.

questions.question: Which detail is part of checking a graph display?
options: The color of the classroom wall
The graph's title, labels, units, and scale
The length of the report title only
questions.explanation: A graph should be read through its title, labels, units, categories, and scale.

questions.question: In the statement "36 out of 60 learners chose option A," enter the total number of learners surveyed.
questions.explanation: The total surveyed is the denominator, 60 learners.

questions.question: A report about all Grade 10 learners uses responses from only one section. What is the best concern to raise?
options: The sample may not represent all Grade 10 learners.
The claim must be true because one section answered.
The display should not include numbers.
questions.explanation: One section may differ from the whole grade level, so the sample may not represent the population named in the claim.

questions.question: A graph compares 51% and 54%, but the vertical axis starts at 50%. In one sentence, explain why the graph may be misleading.
questions.correctAnswer: Starting the axis at 50% can make a small 3 percentage-point difference look much larger than it is.
questions.explanation: Cut-off scales can exaggerate visual differences, so the exact values should be checked.

questions.question: Write a careful conclusion for this result: 28 out of 40 surveyed learners prefer group study.
questions.correctAnswer: The data show that 28 of 40 surveyed learners, or 70%, prefer group study, so the claim is supported for the surveyed group.
questions.explanation: A strong conclusion includes the statistic, the surveyed group, and whether the claim is supported.
